records.source: ר֛וּחַ אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֖ה עָלָ֑י יַ֡עַן מָשַׁח֩ יְהוָ֨ה אֹתִ֜י לְבַשֵּׂ֣ר עֲנָוִ֗ים שְׁלָחַ֨נִי֙ לַחֲבֹ֣שׁ לְנִשְׁבְּרֵי־לֵ֔ב לִקְרֹ֤א לִשְׁבוּיִם֙ דְּר֔וֹר וְלַאֲסוּרִ֖ים פְּקַח־קֽוֹחַ׃
records.gloss: [The] Spirit of [the] Lord Yahweh [is] on me, because Yahweh has anointed me to bring good news to [the] humble; he has sent me to bind up [the] broken of heart, to proclaim to captives liberty, and to [those] bound opening-opening,
pieces: The Spirit of the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} rests on me, \q for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has anointed me to carry good news to the lowly. \q He has sent me to bandage hearts that are broken, \q to announce freedom for captives and, for those in chains, eyes opened wide,

L.1: [The] Spirit of the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} [is] upon me, \q because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has anointed me to bring good news to [the] lowly; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has sent me to bind up [the] broken of heart, \q to proclaim to captives release, and to [those] bound, [eyes] opened wide,

R.1: The Spirit of the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} is on me. \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has anointed me, choosing me for this work. He sent me to bring good news to poor people. \q He sent me to heal people whose hearts are broken. \q He sent me to tell captives that they are free, and to tell prisoners that they will see the light again.

decisions.choice: the speaker is one anointed and sent by the LORD, who is not named
decisions.reason: Someone speaks of himself. He may be the prophet, sent with God's message (48:16). He may be the servant of the LORD, on whom God put his Spirit (42:1) and who was sent to open blind eyes and free prisoners (42:7; 49:9). In Luke 4:16-21 Jesus reads these words in the synagogue at Nazareth and says, "Today this scripture has been fulfilled in your hearing."

decisions.choice: anointed: set apart by God for a task, here by the gift of his Spirit
decisions.reason: Kings, priests and sometimes prophets were anointed with oil for their office (1 Samuel 16:13; Exodus 28:41; 1 Kings 19:16). Here the anointing goes with the Spirit resting on the speaker, as with David in 1 Samuel 16:13 and the shoot of Jesse in 11:2.

decisions.choice: release: the freeing of slaves in the year of jubilee
decisions.reason: The word is used for the release proclaimed in the jubilee year (Leviticus 25:10) and for freeing slaves (Jeremiah 34:8, 15, 17). Verse 2 continues the picture with "a year of favor".

decisions.choice: eyes opened wide: a doubled word for complete opening, used of eyes
alternatives: the opening of the prison to those who are bound
recovery of sight to the blind
decisions.reason: The verb behind it is used of opening the eyes (42:7, 20), and prisoners led out of a dark dungeon see light again (42:7). Some take it as the opening of the prison itself. The Septuagint has "recovery of sight to the blind" here, and Luke 4:18 quotes that wording; Luke 4:18 also includes "to set free the oppressed", words from 58:6.

decisions.choice: choosing me for this work
decisions.reason: Readable explains what being anointed means (see m2).

records.heading: Good news for the lowly

records.source: לִקְרֹ֤א שְׁנַת־רָצוֹן֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה וְי֥וֹם נָקָ֖ם לֵאלֹהֵ֑ינוּ לְנַחֵ֖ם כָּל־אֲבֵלִֽים׃
records.gloss: to proclaim a year of favor of Yahweh and a day of vengeance of our God, to comfort all mourners,
pieces: to announce a year when {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} shows favor \q and a day when our God takes vengeance, \q to console all who grieve,

L.2: to proclaim a year of favor of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} \q and a day of vengeance of our God, \q to comfort all [who] mourn,

R.2: He sent me to announce that the time has come for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to show kindness. \q It is the day for our God to punish {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} enemies. \q He sent me to comfort everyone who is sad.

decisions.choice: a year of favor of the LORD: a time of grace that recalls the jubilee year
decisions.reason: With "release" in verse 1, the words recall the jubilee, the year in which debts were cancelled, land returned and slaves set free (Leviticus 25:8-13). The word "favor" is the same as in 49:8 ("in a time of favor I have answered you") and 60:10.

decisions.choice: a day of vengeance: the day God brings justice against those who oppressed his people
decisions.reason: Vengeance in these chapters is God's just repayment of Zion's enemies, which is the other side of her rescue (34:8; 35:4; 59:17-18; 63:4). A year of favor is set beside a day of vengeance: the favor lasts far longer.

decisions.choice: Luke 4:19 stops before "a day of vengeance"
decisions.reason: When Jesus reads this passage in Luke 4:18-19, he ends with the year of the Lord's favor and closes the scroll.

decisions.choice: to punish his enemies
decisions.reason: Readable says who the vengeance is against, as the context shows (59:18; 63:4).

records.source: לָשׂ֣וּם׀לַאֲבֵלֵ֣י צִיּ֗וֹן לָתֵת֩ לָהֶ֨ם פְּאֵ֜ר תַּ֣חַת אֵ֗פֶר שֶׁ֤מֶן שָׂשׂוֹן֙ תַּ֣חַת אֵ֔בֶל מַעֲטֵ֣ה תְהִלָּ֔ה תַּ֖חַת ר֣וּחַ כֵּהָ֑ה וְקֹרָ֤א לָהֶם֙ אֵילֵ֣י הַצֶּ֔דֶק מַטַּ֥ע יְהוָ֖ה לְהִתְפָּאֵֽר׃
records.gloss: to put for [the] mourners of Zion, to give to them a turban instead of ashes, oil of joy instead of mourning, a mantle of praise instead of a faint spirit; and it will be called to them oaks of righteousness, [the] planting of Yahweh, to glorify himself.
pieces: to provide for those who mourn in Zion, to give them a festive turban in place of ashes, \q the oil of rejoicing in place of grief, \q a cloak of praise in place of a spirit burning low. \q They will be named oaks of righteousness, \q planted by {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to show {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} beauty.

L.3: to provide for [the] mourners of Zion, to give them a turban instead of ashes, \q oil of joy instead of mourning, \q a wrap of praise instead of a dim spirit; \q and they will be called oaks of righteousness, \q the planting of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, to show {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} beauty.

R.3: He sent me to care for those in Zion who are mourning. \q They have ashes on their heads, but they will get a beautiful turban to wear. \q They are grieving, but they will receive oil that brings joy. \q Their spirits are weak, but they will be dressed in praise like a coat. \q People will call them great oak trees of righteousness. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} planted them to show {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} beauty.

decisions.choice: a turban instead of ashes, oil of joy instead of mourning: the signs of mourning replaced by the dress of a celebration
decisions.reason: Mourners put ashes or dust on their heads (2 Samuel 13:19) and did not anoint themselves with oil (2 Samuel 14:2). At a feast people wore a fine headdress and put oil on their heads (Psalm 23:5; 45:8). The words for "turban" and "ashes" sound alike in Hebrew, and the same turban is worn by the bridegroom in verse 10.

decisions.choice: a dim spirit: a spirit that is faint and failing
decisions.reason: The word means dim or faint; it is used of the dimly burning wick in 42:3 and of failing eyes (Genesis 27:1).

decisions.choice: oaks of righteousness, the planting of the LORD: strong trees that God has planted, showing his beauty
decisions.reason: Oaks or terebinths are large, long-lived trees. In 1:29-30 the people were ashamed of the sacred oaks of idol worship; now they themselves are oaks marked by righteousness. "The planting of the LORD" and "to show his beauty" repeat 60:21. Grammar: the first verb in the verse ("to provide") has no object; the next phrase says what is given.

decisions.choice: They have ashes on their heads ... dressed in praise like a coat
decisions.reason: Readable spells out each exchange in short sentences and explains that the ashes were on their heads (see m1).

records.source: וּבָנוּ֙ חָרְב֣וֹת עוֹלָ֔ם שֹׁמְמ֥וֹת רִֽאשֹׁנִ֖ים יְקוֹמֵ֑מוּ וְחִדְּשׁוּ֙ עָ֣רֵי חֹ֔רֶב שֹׁמְמ֖וֹת דּ֥וֹר וָדֽוֹר׃
records.gloss: And they will build [the] ruins of antiquity; [the] desolations of [the] former [ones] they will raise up; and they will renew [the] cities of ruin, [the] desolations of generation and generation.
pieces: They will build up what has lain in ruins since long ago \q and restore places left empty in their ancestors' time; \q they will make new again the wrecked cities, \q deserted for one generation after another.

L.4: And they will build [the] ruins of long ago; \q [the] desolations of former [times] they will raise up; \q and they will renew [the] cities of ruin, \q [the] desolations of generation and generation.

R.4: They will rebuild the old ruins. \q They will repair places that were destroyed long ago. \q They will make the ruined towns new again, \q towns that have been empty for many years.

decisions.choice: they: the mourners of Zion, now restored
decisions.reason: The people who were mourning in verse 3 are the ones who rebuild. In verse 5 foreigners serve them.

decisions.choice: rebuilding the ancient ruins: the promise of 58:12 and 49:8
decisions.reason: In 58:12 those who keep God's ways "will build the ancient ruins". The promise answers 44:26, where God says of Judah's towns, "they will be rebuilt" (compare Amos 9:14).

records.source: וְעָמְד֣וּ זָרִ֔ים וְרָע֖וּ צֹאנְכֶ֑ם וּבְנֵ֣י נֵכָ֔ר אִכָּרֵיכֶ֖ם וְכֹרְמֵיכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And strangers will stand and shepherd your flocks, and sons of foreignness [will be] your farmers and your vinedressers.
pieces: Outsiders will stand ready to pasture your flocks, \q and people from foreign lands will plow your fields and tend your vines.

L.5: And strangers will stand and shepherd your flocks, \q and sons of a foreign land [will be] your plowmen and your vinedressers.

R.5: People from other countries will come and take care of your sheep. \q Foreigners will plow your fields and take care of your grapevines.

decisions.choice: your: now plural, addressed to the people of Zion
decisions.reason: From here to verse 7 the people are addressed as "you" (plural), not the city as "you" (feminine singular) as in chapter 60.

decisions.choice: foreigners doing the work: the people freed to serve God as priests
decisions.reason: Once strangers devoured the land (1:7); now they tend its flocks and fields. This frees Israel for the priestly work of verse 6 (compare 14:2; 60:10).

records.source: וְאַתֶּ֗ם כֹּהֲנֵ֤י יְהוָה֙ תִּקָּרֵ֔אוּ מְשָׁרְתֵ֣י אֱלֹהֵ֔ינוּ יֵאָמֵ֖ר לָכֶ֑ם חֵ֤יל גּוֹיִם֙ תֹּאכֵ֔לוּ וּבִכְבוֹדָ֖ם תִּתְיַמָּֽרוּ׃
records.gloss: And you, priests of Yahweh you will be called; servants of our God it will be said of you; [the] wealth of nations you will eat, and in their glory you will boast.
pieces: And you will be known as priests of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; \q people will speak of you as those who serve our God. \q You will live on the wealth of the nations \q and take pride in their glory.

L.6: But you, [the] priests of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} you will be called; \q servants of our God it will be said of you; \q [the] wealth of nations you will eat, \q and in their glory you will boast.

R.6: You will be called priests of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q People will say that you serve our God. \q You will enjoy the riches of the nations, \q and their glory will make you proud.

decisions.choice: priests of the LORD: the whole people serving God as priests among the nations
decisions.reason: At Sinai God called Israel "a kingdom of priests" (Exodus 19:6). The promise is taken up for the church in 1 Peter 2:9 and Revelation 1:6; 5:10. In 66:21 God takes some even from the nations as priests.

decisions.choice: in their glory you will boast: you will take pride in the riches of the nations
alternatives: you will take over their glory
decisions.reason: "Glory" here means wealth and splendor, as in 66:12. The verb is rare; it is usually taken as "boast" (Psalm 94:4). It may instead come from a verb meaning "exchange", giving "you will take over their glory".

records.source: תַּ֤חַת בָּשְׁתְּכֶם֙ מִשְׁנֶ֔ה וּכְלִמָּ֖ה יָרֹ֣נּוּ חֶלְקָ֑ם לָכֵ֤ן בְּאַרְצָם֙ מִשְׁנֶ֣ה יִירָ֔שׁוּ שִׂמְחַ֥ת עוֹלָ֖ם תִּֽהְיֶ֥ה לָהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: Instead of your shame, double; and [instead of] disgrace they will shout for joy [over] their portion; therefore in their land double they will possess; joy of perpetuity will be to them.
pieces: In place of your shame you will have a double share; \q instead of disgrace they will sing out over what is given them. \q So in their own land they will take possession of a double share, \q and joy that never ends will belong to them.

L.7: In place of your shame, double; \q and [in place of] disgrace they will shout for joy [over] their share; \q therefore in their land double they will possess; \q joy forever will be theirs.

R.7: You were put to shame, but now you will receive twice as much. \q You were disgraced, but now they will shout for joy over what they receive. \q In their land they will receive twice as much as before. \q Their joy will last forever.

decisions.choice: double: a double share, like the portion of a firstborn son
decisions.reason: The firstborn received a double share of the inheritance (Deuteronomy 21:17). In 40:2 Jerusalem received double for her sins; now she receives double in blessing.

decisions.choice: your ... they: the verse moves from "you" to "they" without warning
decisions.reason: Hebrew poetry often changes person in this way; both refer to the people of Zion. The lines are short and leave words to be supplied: "instead of" carries over to "disgrace".

decisions.choice: twice as much; twice as much as before
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what "double" means.

records.source: כִּ֣י אֲנִ֤י יְהוָה֙ אֹהֵ֣ב מִשְׁפָּ֔ט שֹׂנֵ֥א גָזֵ֖ל בְּעוֹלָ֑ה וְנָתַתִּ֤י פְעֻלָּתָם֙ בֶּאֱמֶ֔ת וּבְרִ֥ית עוֹלָ֖ם אֶכְר֥וֹת לָהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: For I Yahweh [am] loving justice, hating robbery with injustice; and I will give their wage in faithfulness, and a covenant of perpetuity I will make with them.
pieces: For I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, am a lover of justice \q and I hate robbery joined to wrongdoing. \q I will pay them their wages faithfully \q and make a covenant with them that lasts forever.

L.8: For I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, love justice; \q I hate robbery with wrongdoing; \q and I will give their wages in faithfulness, \q and a covenant forever I will make with them.

R.8: I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, love what is fair. \q I hate stealing and every kind of wrong. \q I will be faithful and give {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people what they have earned. \q I will make a covenant with them that will last forever.

decisions.choice: robbery with wrongdoing: the vowels of the Masoretic text read "wrongdoing"
decisions.reason: The same consonants can be read "burnt offering", giving "robbery in a burnt offering" (an offering made from stolen goods; compare 1:11-17; Malachi 1:13). The vowels of the Masoretic text give "wrongdoing", and the Septuagint is reported to read it the same way (from memory; to be checked).

decisions.choice: their wages; a covenant forever: God will faithfully give his people what is due to them and bind himself to them for good
decisions.reason: "Wages" here means the reward God gives (40:10; 49:4; 62:11). The everlasting covenant is promised in 55:3 and Jeremiah 32:40.

decisions.choice: my people
decisions.reason: Readable names "them" as God's people, as the context shows.

records.source: וְנוֹדַ֤ע בַּגּוֹיִם֙ זַרְעָ֔ם וְצֶאֱצָאֵיהֶ֖ם בְּת֣וֹךְ הָעַמִּ֑ים כָּל־רֹֽאֵיהֶם֙ יַכִּיר֔וּם כִּ֛י הֵ֥ם זֶ֖רַע בֵּרַ֥ךְ יְהוָֽה׃ס
records.gloss: And will be known among the nations their offspring, and their descendants in [the] midst of the peoples; all [who] see them will recognize them, that they [are] offspring [whom] Yahweh has blessed.
pieces: Their children will be famous among the nations, \q and their descendants among the peoples. \q Anyone who sees them will recognize them \q as a line of children whom {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has blessed.

L.9: And their offspring will be known among the nations, \q and their descendants amid the peoples; \q all who see them will recognize them, \q that they [are] offspring [that] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has blessed.

R.9: Their children and grandchildren will be famous among the nations. \q Everyone who sees them will know that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has blessed them.

decisions.choice: offspring the LORD has blessed: the promise to Abraham fulfilled
decisions.reason: God promised to bless Abraham's offspring and make them a blessing to the nations (Genesis 12:2-3; 22:17-18). In 65:23 the people are again "offspring blessed by the LORD".

records.source: שׂ֧וֹשׂ אָשִׂ֣ישׂ בַּֽיהוָ֗ה תָּגֵ֤ל נַפְשִׁי֙ בֵּֽאלֹהַ֔י כִּ֤י הִלְבִּישַׁ֨נִי֙ בִּגְדֵי־יֶ֔שַׁע מְעִ֥יל צְדָקָ֖ה יְעָטָ֑נִי כֶּֽחָתָן֙ יְכַהֵ֣ן פְּאֵ֔ר וְכַכַּלָּ֖ה תַּעְדֶּ֥ה כֵלֶֽיהָ׃
records.gloss: Rejoicing I will rejoice in Yahweh; will exult my soul in my God, for he has clothed me [in] garments of salvation; [with] a robe of righteousness he has wrapped me, like a bridegroom [who] acts as priest [with] a turban, and like a bride [who] adorns [herself with] her jewels.
pieces: My joy in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} overflows; my whole being delights in my God. \q He has dressed me in clothing of salvation \q and wrapped me in a cloak of righteousness, \q like a bridegroom wearing a turban as a priest does, \q like a bride decked out in her jewels.

L.10: Rejoicing I will rejoice in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; my soul will exult in my God, \q for {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has clothed me [in] garments of salvation; \q [in] a robe of righteousness {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has wrapped me, \q as a bridegroom serves as priest [with] a turban, \q and as a bride adorns [herself with] her jewelry.

R.10: I am filled with joy because of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. With all my heart I celebrate my God. \q He has dressed me in salvation like new clothes. \q He has wrapped me in righteousness like a coat. \q I am like a bridegroom wearing a fine turban like a priest. \q I am like a bride putting on her jewelry.

decisions.choice: the speaker: Zion, or the anointed one of verse 1, rejoicing in what God has done
decisions.reason: The speaker is not named. It may be Zion or her people answering the promises (compare the bride in 49:18; 62:5). It may be the anointed one of verses 1-3 speaking again. The joy is the same either way: God has clothed the speaker in salvation.

decisions.choice: garments of salvation, a robe of righteousness: God gives his people the clothing he himself wears
decisions.reason: In 59:17 the LORD puts on righteousness as armor and salvation as a helmet. Priests are clothed with salvation and righteousness in Psalm 132:9, 16. Revelation 19:7-8 and 21:2 picture the bride of the Lamb dressed for her wedding.

decisions.choice: serves as priest with a turban: the bridegroom puts on a fine headdress like a priest's
decisions.reason: The verb comes from the word for priest. The word for turban is used of the priests' headdresses (Exodus 39:28) and of the mourners' new turban in verse 3.

decisions.choice: My joy overflows / I am filled with joy
decisions.reason: The verb is doubled for emphasis; Balanced and Readable express the emphasis without the repetition that Literal keeps.

records.heading: Dressed in salvation

records.source: כִּ֤י כָאָ֨רֶץ֙ תּוֹצִ֣יא צִמְחָ֔הּ וּכְגַנָּ֖ה זֵרוּעֶ֣יהָ תַצְמִ֑יחַ כֵּ֣ן׀אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֗ה יַצְמִ֤יחַ צְדָקָה֙ וּתְהִלָּ֔ה נֶ֖גֶד כָּל־הַגּוֹיִֽם׃
records.gloss: For like the earth [that] brings forth its growth, and like a garden [that] makes its sown things sprout, so [the] Lord Yahweh will make sprout righteousness and praise before all the nations.
pieces: As the ground pushes up its new growth, \q as a garden makes its seeds break through the soil, \q so the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} will make righteousness and praise grow up in full view of every nation.

L.11: For like the earth [that] brings out its shoots, \q and like a garden [that] makes its sown [seeds] spring up, \q so the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} will make spring up righteousness and praise before all the nations.

R.11: Plants come up out of the ground, and seeds grow in a garden. \q In the same way, the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} will make righteousness and praise grow. \q All the nations will see it.

decisions.choice: make righteousness spring up: God makes right order and rescue grow among his people, as surely as plants grow
decisions.reason: "Righteousness" here includes the setting right of Zion's cause (62:1-2). The picture of righteousness sprouting appears in 45:8 and Psalm 85:12.

decisions.choice: the growth is God's work, seen by all nations
decisions.reason: Just as soil and garden bring up what is planted in them, the Lord GOD causes the growth; the nations see it and praise follows (60:3; 62:2).
